# itakeit-agent

> itakeit-agent is a free, self-hosted Claude agent for itakeit's Slack channels. It claims the tasks its configured skills cover and works them in the task thread the way a person does: it reacts 🙋 to claim, says what it will do, replies with the result, and sets ✅ done, ❓ needs info or ⛔ blocked.

It runs as one Docker container on Claude, through the Claude Code CLI and its login or through the Messages API with an API key. It connects to Slack over Socket Mode, so it needs no public URL, and it keeps no database: its state is its own reactions in the channel. It never talks to itakeit directly; itakeit sees it as one more user, so every itakeit rule applies to it unchanged.

## How it works

- After claim_delay_seconds (0 unless set; the example config uses 120), if nobody claimed a new task, the agent asks Claude whether its skills cover it. If so, it claims it and works it.
- Knowledge files (runbooks, architecture notes, FAQs) are sent with every request, cached, as trusted facts.
- A reply to its ❓ or ⛔, or a mention on any task it owns, starts another round with the whole thread.
- Without tools it takes only tasks a written reply completes.
- Propose mode: it investigates with read-only tools the operator lists (Bash command patterns such as kubectl get, file tools confined to a per-task directory, MCP tools) and proposes the change for a human to apply.
- Fix mode: it also runs write entries. Each write is posted in the thread before it runs; with an approver set, it runs only after that Slack user reacts ✔️ on the approval message.
- Every tool call goes to the agent for a decision; the Claude CLI runs nothing on its own. The CLI gets an allow-listed environment without the Slack tokens, and known secret values are scrubbed from replies, best effort. Anything a read entry can read can end up quoted in the channel.
- Fix mode without an approver requires allow_unapproved_writes: true. Tools require the claude-code backend. The image carries only the Claude CLI; the repository's examples add kubectl (examples/kubectl), gcloud for GKE (examples/gcloud), or run the agent in Kubernetes with its ServiceAccount (examples/in-cluster).
- Fix mode gives every tool session a fresh home directory and copies the kubeconfig named in KUBECONFIG into it; allow_real_home: true keeps the real one, with an approver. Read entries that can print or change credentials (Bash(kubectl *), kubectl config, gcloud auth and similar) are refused, and so is every tool call with a flag such as --insecure-skip-tls-verify or --kubeconfig.

## Memory (advanced, optional)

- An additional feature, off by default, that runs only in the separate itakeit-agent-mem image (ghcr.io/nice-pink/itakeit-agent-mem, built from Dockerfile.mem). The regular image refuses to start with memory enabled and names that image. It works with every mode and both backends.
- It uses poma-memory (https://github.com/poma-ai/poma-memory): local keyword and semantic search over Markdown files, with a small embedding model baked into the image, no API key and no network at run time.
- Before triage and every work round, the agent searches its memory for the task and adds matching notes to the request. They are marked as notes from earlier Slack threads, hints and never instructions, and are kept apart from the trusted knowledge files. When nothing matches well it adds nothing; at startup it checks that this relevance filter works and refuses to start otherwise.
- When a task ends ✅, the agent can propose a learning. With approval (the default, agent.memory.approval: true) it posts the learning in the thread and saves it only after the approver reacts ✔️; ❌ drops it. Requests are signed, so a reply made to look like one saves nothing, and they still count after a restart. With approval: false it saves learnings without review.
- Learnings are stored as Markdown in learnings/YYYY-MM.md in the memory directory, next to any notes the operator adds there. The search index is a SQLite file rebuilt from the Markdown, so the Markdown is what to back up. The memory directory needs a writable volume.

## Setup

1. Run itakeit in the channel (https://itakeit.nice.pink).
2. Create a separate Slack app from the manifest in the repository (scopes: channels:history, groups:history, channels:read, groups:read, chat:write, reactions:read, reactions:write; events: message.channels, message.groups, reaction_added, member_joined_channel, member_left_channel, channel_left, group_left, channel_archive, group_archive, channel_unarchive, group_unarchive). Generate an app-level token with connections:write (AGENT_SLACK_APP_TOKEN) and install the app (AGENT_SLACK_BOT_TOKEN).
3. Invite it to itakeit's channels and add an agent block (itakeit_app, the itakeit app's App ID; skills) to itakeit's config.yaml. The agent works in the same channels as itakeit, from that shared config: a channels list (or a single channel), or auto_channels: true for every channel the agent is a member of, so inviting it adds a channel and removing it stops it there.
4. Run claude setup-token for CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, or use backend: api with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
5. Run the published image ghcr.io/nice-pink/itakeit-agent (amd64 and arm64; latest follows main) with the tokens and the config mounted, or build it from the repository. Docker Compose files in the repository run it next to itakeit.
6. Check the log for "connected to slack", then post a task the skills cover.
